title: Optimize Console: Chronicle view for recommendation cards, diff preview, and safe-apply replay
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background:
Redwood Optimize currently surfaces batching and KV caching recommendations but lacks a concise, auditable journey for operators to preview diffs, perform safe applies, and inspect post-apply outcomes. Customers managing Dedicated and Private deployments require an immutable audit trail and reproducible rollback steps for compliance and incident response.

Goal:
Ship a Chronicle UX in the Console Optimize surface that unifies: (1) recommendation cards with confidence signals and estimated cost delta, (2) a side-by-side diff preview (dry-run), and (3) an apply history / replayable audit trail that includes snapshots, traffic routing used during apply, validation failures, and an easy rollback flow.

Scope (MVP):
- Recommendation cards redesigned to include: observed token distribution, estimated cost impact, risk score, and quick actions (Preview Diff, Dry-Run, Apply, Schedule).
- Diff preview modal: side-by-side config changes, textual explanation, expanded policy impacts (routing, quantization), and a simulated cost/latency projection for 1h/24h workload.
- Apply workflow: include an explicit Dry-Run toggle that records a pre-apply snapshot, stores per-request sample logs for the trial, and marks the apply result as Success/Partial/Failed with reason.
- Apply History (Chronicle): chronological list of applies with filters (by model, team, user, time), ability to open a recorded run to replay the diff preview, view the exact snapshot used for rollback, and trigger a rollback with optional canary percent.
- Audit details: who initiated apply, git diff / config commit link, change set id, validation checklist, and links to related PRs and dashboards.

Out of scope (future): automated A/B metric analysis, multi-tenant cross-apply rollups, per-token sample playback in UI (server work will instrument).

Acceptance criteria:
1) PM/Design/ENG sign-off on card info architecture and diff preview layout (Figma mock linked).
2) Dry-run persistently stores a snapshot that can be promoted to a real apply or discarded.
3) Apply History supports filtering and shows at least: initiator, timestamp, change delta summary, and link to snapshot.
4) Rollback flow uses stored snapshot and allows specifying canary percent and notes; triggers a background job with progress updates surfaced in Console.
5) Audit export: ability to download JSON of one apply event including request samples and validation logs.
6) No regression in Console performance (page load < 2s for 50 recent applies).

UX details and design links:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/REDWOOD/optimize-chronicle-mvp (mock prototype, see pages "Cards v3" & "Diff Modal")
- Confluence PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Optimize+Chronicle+PRD
- Example GH PR for server snapshot API: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1189

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Snapshot retention: default 90 days vs 365 days for enterprise customers (cost vs compliance). Recommend 90 days for MVP and enterprise opt-in.
- Snapshot size: store compressed config + 1000 request samples vs full request bodies. Engineering prefers trimmed samples to avoid PII risk.
- Rollback semantics: immediate switch vs canary rollout. Default to canary 10% for Dedicated customers; provide override for emergency full rollback.

Telemetry and observability:
- New events: optimize.recommendation.preview, optimize.apply.started, optimize.apply.completed, optimize.apply.rollback.requested.
- Instrument latency and cost-estimate accuracy metrics to measure recommendation value (actual vs estimated cost over 72h).

Success metrics:
- 30% reduction in manual rollback incidents for Optimize applies within 3 months of GA.
- 20% of recommendations applied via Console (vs API) within 6 weeks of release.
- Audit export used in at least 3 enterprise support escalations in first quarter.

Implementation notes for ENG:
- Backend: add snapshot API (create/list/get/promote/rollback) and attach snapshot_id to apply events.
- UI: new Chronicle list page under Optimize, card components, diff modal, progress toast and background job polling endpoint.
- Security: snapshots must respect KMS encryption at rest and RBAC checks at retrieval time.

Deliverables:
- High-fidelity mocks for card variants and diff modal (Design).
- Snapshot API and migration plan (Backend).
- Chronicle Console pages and interactions (Frontend).
- E2E test plan for dry-run -> apply -> rollback flow (QA).

Notes for handoff:
- Design tokens and spacing consistent with Console v2 components.
- Provide example API requests and cURL snippets to mirror UI actions for auditability.
- Link to runtime change that adds per-request sampling for dry-run: ENG-94500.
